operations.content: TrackFlow is a two-country last-mile delivery and warehouse management company whose AI Engineering project builds systems and automations for logistics operations.
The project serves warehouse operations, carrier management, reverse logistics, customer experience, commercial teams, technology, and executive leadership across Los Angeles and Zaragoza.
Planned capabilities include unified inventory, order ingestion, carrier selection and tracking, returns automation, CX assistance, telemetry, dashboards, workflows, and executive reporting.
TrackFlow operates across the United States and Spain with separate warehouse systems, eight carriers, English and Spanish needs, and legacy undocumented integrations.

The repository is a monorepo organized by responsibility: uis for interfaces, services for the centralized API, data for pipelines, agents for AI, workflows for orchestration, and infra/scripts/internal for operations.
The documented backend direction is one centralized FastAPI company API with domain routers, adding separate workers only when background execution truly requires it.
The intended data flow is raw source data through pipelines into processed outputs, which are consumed by services, UIs, or agents; evaluation data belongs in data/eval.
The repository currently has a private TypeScript shared package named @repo/shared-types at version 0.0.1, with index.ts as its main and type entry point.
The repository is currently a documentation and folder-structure skeleton; no root workspace runner or runnable applications are configured yet.
Memory-bank maintenance uses python3 .agents/skills/memory-bank/scripts/memory.py with init, apply, validate, find, consolidate, stats, index, and rollback commands.
Each new app, service, agent, or pipeline should live in its own subfolder and include a README documenting what was added and how it is used.

Place work according to responsibility: user interfaces in uis, APIs and background services in services, data movement in data/pipelines, AI assistants in agents, and reusable AI capabilities in skills.
The capstone company is TrackFlow because its logistics, data engineering, telemetry, resilience, and automation problems are considered relevant and realistic.
The initial AI agent idea is a carrier recommender that uses package weight, destination, and urgency to recommend the optimal carrier.
The project has selected TrackFlow and populated CONTEXT.md; the repository remains at the starter-template stage with documentation and empty implementation folders.
Define the first implementation milestone, prioritizing centralized telemetry and logging or digitized warehouse restocking, then establish the required application structure.
